## Why This Is Asked

This question probes the ability to design end-to-end testing for data contracts in a real-time pipeline, including schema evolution across multiple producers and downstream consumers. It emphasizes concrete testing layers, measurable SLIs, and safe rollback paths, which are critical for large-scale data platforms at Google, Cloudflare, and Plaid.

- Data quality gates and drift detection
- Shadow/canary testing and replayable datasets

// Minimal contract test sketch: backward compatibility check
function isBackwardCompatible(oldSchema, newSchema, sampleEvent) {
  const oldOk = parseWithSchema(sampleEvent, oldSchema);
  const newOk = parseWithSchema(sampleEvent, newSchema);
  return oldOk && newOk;
}
```

// Example: simple TTL cache skeleton used for tests
class Cache { constructor() { this.store = new Map(); } set(key, value, ttlMs) { const expiry = Date.now() + ttlMs; this.store.set(key, { value, expiry }); } get(key) { const entry = this.store.get(key); if (!entry) return null; if (Date.now() > entry.expiry) { this.store.delete(key); return null; } return entry.value; } }
```

## Why This Is Asked

In fintech-like domains, event-sourced architectures are common and replay safety critical. This question probes experience with end-to-end validation, idempotency, and exactly-once guarantees under stress.

## Key Concepts

- Event sourcing and CQRS
- Idempotent event handlers and deduplication
- Exactly-once processing and out-of-order delivery
- Replay scenarios, rollback, and read-model consistency

## Code Example

```javascript
function applyEvent(state, event) {
  const id = event.aggregateId + ':' + event.sequence
  if (state.seen && state.seen[id]) return state // idempotent guard
  // apply logic depending on event.type
  const next = { ...state, data: {/* updated */}, seen: { ...(state.seen || {}), [id]: true } }
  return next
}
```

- How would you simulate out-of-order delivery and replay in CI?
- What metrics and dashboards would you use to detect drift between write models and read models?

def kl_div(p, q):
    return sum(pi * math.log(pi/qi) for pi, qi in zip(p, q) if pi > 0 and qi > 0)

def drift_exceeds(p, q, thr=0.1):
